test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which year was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1990**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** serves as the apex regulatory body for overseeing the licensing and regulation of micro, small, and medium enterprise finance companies in India.
 
• It operates under the purview of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, with its headquarters located in Lucknow and offices across the country.
 
• Established on April 2, 1990, by the Government of India, SIDBI initially operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of IDBI Bank. However, it was delinked from IDBI on March 27, 2000.
 
• SIDBI's primary objective is to provide refinance facilities to banks and financial institutions, as well as offer term lending and working capital finance to industries, particularly those in the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector.
 
• SIDBI coordinates the activities of institutions involved in similar endeavors. Its establishment in 1990 was facilitated through an Act of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• SIDBI is among the five All India Financial Institutions overseen by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI).**
 
• The other four institutions include the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank), National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Housing Bank (NHB), and National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NABFID).
 
• NHB came under government control after the government acquired more than a 51% stake in it. These institutions play a crucial statutory role in the financial markets, particularly through credit extension and refinancing operations, catering to the long-term financing requirements of the industrial sector. SIDBI actively contributes to the development of Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) through the SIDBI Foundation for Micro Credit.
 
• It supports the extension of microfinance through the Micro Finance Institution (MFI) route, demonstrating its commitment to fostering financial inclusion and supporting the growth of small businesses.
